title: Admin approval dashboard with super_admin vs helper_admin role separation

requirements.text: Update the role model to use exactly these roles everywhere the app checks or displays role: `super_admin`, `helper_admin`, `user` (remove/stop using the legacy `admin` role in UI logic and guards).
acceptanceCriteria: The codebase no longer uses `role === 'admin'` as the condition for admin access; admin access is based on `super_admin` or `helper_admin`.
TypeScript types that represent a user profile role include `helper_admin` and do not require an `admin` role.

requirements.text: Enforce admin-route access rules so that only `super_admin` and `helper_admin` can access `/admin/users`, and normal users cannot access any admin routes.

quotes:
Access rules:
- Only super_admin and helper_admin can access /admin/users
- Normal users cannot access admin routes

acceptanceCriteria: Navigating directly to `/admin/users` as a `user` does not render the page and redirects to a non-admin route (use the existing unauthorized behavior pattern).
Navigating to `/admin/users` as `super_admin` or `helper_admin` renders the admin users dashboard.
Any existing admin navigation entry points (e.g., profile menu) only appear for `super_admin`/`helper_admin`, not for `user`.

requirements.text: Create/adjust the Admin Users Dashboard at route `/admin/users` to show a **Pending** list that only includes Firestore `users` documents where `approved == false` (do not show already-approved users in this list).

quotes: Create an Admin Users Dashboard at /admin/users.
Show only users where approved = false in Pending list

acceptanceCriteria: `/admin/users` displays only users with `approved === false`.
If there are no pending users, the screen shows an empty state message indicating there are no pending users.
The list data is fetched from the Firestore `users` collection (using the existing Firestore wrapper/hook pattern).

requirements.text:
Implement strict field-level visibility on `/admin/users`:
- `super_admin` can see: profile photo, name, age, relation, phone number, email, role, approval status
- `helper_admin` can see ONLY: profile photo, name, age, relation, approval status
- `helper_admin` must not see: phone number, email, role-change options, delete options

quotes:
Data visibility rules:
- super_admin can see:
  - profile photo
  - name
  - age
  - relation
  - phone number
  - email
  - role
  - approval status

- helper_admin can see ONLY:
  - profile photo
  - name
  - age
  - relation
  - approval status

- helper_admin MUST NOT see:
  - phone number
  - email
  - role change options
  - delete options

acceptanceCriteria: When logged in as `helper_admin`, the users table does not render phone, email, or role columns/values anywhere on the page.
When logged in as `helper_admin`, there is no UI control to change a user role and no UI control to delete a user.
When logged in as `super_admin`, all specified fields (including phone, email, role) are visible in the pending list.
Approval status is visible to both admin roles.

requirements.text:
Implement admin actions on pending users with strict role separation:
- `super_admin`: Approve user, Reject user, Block user, Promote user to `helper_admin`
- `helper_admin`: Approve user, Reject user
Also ensure the UI does not expose disallowed actions to `helper_admin` and does not allow `helper_admin` to execute role changes or deletion via any client-side path.

quotes:
Actions:
- super_admin:
  - Approve user
  - Reject user
  - Block user
  - Promote user to helper_admin

- helper_admin:
  - Approve user
  - Reject user

Do NOT allow:
- helper_admin to modify roles
- helper_admin to delete users

acceptanceCriteria: As `super_admin`, each pending user row offers actions: Approve, Reject, Block, Promote to helper_admin (with confirmation dialogs consistent with existing patterns).
As `helper_admin`, each pending user row offers only: Approve and Reject.
Attempting to trigger role updates as `helper_admin` is not possible via the UI (no action items rendered).
No delete-user functionality is added as part of this change.

requirements.text:
Persist approval/rejection/block state in Firestore so login behavior matches requirements:
- On approval: set `approved = true`
- On rejection: keep `approved = false` and store a rejection flag/status so the app can show “Rejected by admin” on login
- On block: store a block flag/status so the app can prevent login access and show an appropriate message
Keep existing signup flow intact (do not change signup logic).

quotes:
On approval:
- Set approved = true
- Redirect user to chat screen on next login

On rejection:
- Keep approved = false
- Show “Rejected by admin” message on user login

Do not change signup logic.

acceptanceCriteria: Approving a pending user updates the Firestore user document so that subsequent logins route to `/chat` via the existing redirect logic.
Rejecting a pending user leaves `approved === false` and sets a dedicated rejected indicator in Firestore (so the client can distinguish pending vs rejected).
Blocking a user sets a dedicated blocked indicator in Firestore (independent of `approved`).
No changes are made to the signup flow behavior; newly created non-first users remain unapproved by default.

requirements.text: Update the login flow to display the exact message “Rejected by admin” when a user attempts to log in and their Firestore profile indicates they were rejected (while still unapproved). Also prevent blocked users from proceeding past login with a clear English message.

quotes: Show “Rejected by admin” message on user login

acceptanceCriteria: If a user profile is marked rejected, the Login screen shows the exact string “Rejected by admin” and does not navigate into the app.
If a user profile is marked blocked, the Login screen shows an English blocked message and does not navigate into the app.
If a user is unapproved and not rejected, the app follows the existing behavior (routes to `/pending-approval`).
If a user is approved, the app routes to `/chat` using the existing redirect helper.

requirements.text:
Update Firestore security rules (`frontend/firestore.rules`) to support the new `helper_admin` role:
- Allow `helper_admin` to read the users collection as needed for `/admin/users`
- Allow `helper_admin` to update only the minimal fields needed to approve/reject (and never role/phone/email)
- Keep `super_admin` as the only role that can update roles, delete users, or perform privileged updates

quotes: Fetch users from Firestore users collection

helper_admin MUST NOT see:
  - phone number
  - email
  - role change options
  - delete options

acceptanceCriteria: A `helper_admin` can successfully load the pending users list from Firestore without permission errors.
A `helper_admin` can update approval/rejection status for a user but cannot update `role`, `phone`, or `email` fields per Firestore rules.
A `super_admin` can update approval/rejection/block status and can promote a user to `helper_admin`.
A normal `user` still cannot read other users’ profiles and cannot access admin capabilities.

requirements.text: Ensure role privacy in the UI: clearly label roles internally for admins, but do not expose whether any admin is `super_admin` vs `helper_admin` to normal users anywhere in the non-admin UI.

quotes:
UI:
- Clearly label roles internally (not visible to users)
- Users should never know who is super_admin or helper_admin

acceptanceCriteria: In non-admin UI surfaces (e.g., the profile menu), normal users do not see labels that reveal `super_admin` or `helper_admin`.
Admin-only screens may show internal role labels as needed, but normal users cannot infer which admins are `super_admin` vs `helper_admin` from the standard user experience.

constraints: Do not build or expand the chat system beyond ensuring approved users continue to redirect to `/chat` on login.
Do not change the signup logic/flow (including first-user bootstrap behavior).
Helper admins must not be able to modify roles, delete users, or view sensitive fields (phone, email).
Keep all changes within the existing React + Firebase/Firestore frontend; do not introduce additional backend services.
nonGoals: Implementing or redesigning the chat system.
Adding third-party authentication beyond what already exists.
